name: core--proxmox-disk-aio-threads
description: Proxmox VM disks are created with aio=threads instead of the io_uring default, after vm700 threw sporadic EIO under sustained write load and took its 200 GB ext4 filesystem read-only. NOTE: aio was the first hypothesis and did NOT fix it — the real cause was the emulated LSI controller, see eval 033. The setting is kept as sound practice for LVM-thin, not as the fix

implementation.change: asyncio = "threads" on disk-type entries of the dynamic disk block (null for the cloud-init drive), with a comment recording the incident and the fact that ignore_changes = [disk] keeps this from reaching existing VMs

checks: Incident evidence: guest dmesg on 2026-08-16 04:03:34 shows 'I/O error, dev sdb' on multiple sectors, then 'EXT4-fs error (device sdb): Detected aborted journal' and 'Remounting filesystem read-only'

Hardware ruled out: every reported failing sector re-reads without error afterwards, a 200 MiB sequential read runs at 520 MB/s, NVMe SMART reports PASSED, and the lvmthin pool is 40% full (761 GB of 1884 GB) with metadata at 1.7%
Filesystem repaired: e2fsck -fy /dev/sdb corrected an orphaned inode list and free-block/free-inode counts, exit status 1 (errors corrected)
vm700 scsi0 and scsi1 now read local-lvm:vm-700-disk-N,aio=threads,replicate=0,size=... in the Proxmox config
The setting is live, not just pending: VM was shut down (ACPI, 15s) and started again

Post-change boot looked clean at first, but the errors returned on the next heavy run and hit /dev/sda too — so aio was not the cause. Superseded as an explanation by eval 033 (scsihw=lsi bus resets); retained because threads is the safer aio mode on LVM-thin
Provider Telmate/proxmox 3.0.1-rc6 accepts asyncio on the disk block
Terraform module change verified by inspection only: `disk` is in lifecycle.ignore_changes, so no plan/apply against existing VMs was run
